keynotes.name: Yannik Frisch
keynotes.affiliation: Medical Faculty of Heidelberg University, Germany
keynotes.group: Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Cardiovascular Medicine
keynotes.title: From Synthetic Data to Adaptive Data Engines
keynotes.description:
Medical AI systems are often limited not only by too little data, but by long-tailed data distributions, where rare pathologies, configurations and events are poorly represented.
 While modern generative models can produce increasingly realistic medical data, realism alone does not guarantee that synthetic data provides useful information to a downstream discriminative system.
 This keynote examines how generative augmentation can move from uniform sampling toward rare-case, information-guided, and ultimately adaptive data generation.
 Drawing on recent work and own research on surgical image and video generation, I will show how the utility of synthetic data depends strongly on what is generated, where it lies in the data distribution, and how it is selected. 
 I then discuss the limits of these approaches and how structured representations, digital twins, and world models may enable controlled extrapolation for clinically relevant scenarios that are scarcely observed in real datasets.
 The broader vision is to move from static synthetic datasets to adaptive data engines that identify what a learning system is missing, generate valid data to address these gaps, and verify their utility on real downstream tasks.
